high.title: Peso Rebounds as US, Iran Pause Attacks
high.summary: The Philippine Peso staged a sharp recovery on Monday, gaining 17.2 centavos to close at P61.675 per dollar — pulling back from its record-low finish of P61.847 on Friday. The primary catalyst was easing global crude oil prices over the weekend, driven by a temporary pause in hostilities between the US and Iran. A softer oil price environment is materially bullish for the Peso, as the Philippines is a net energy importer; lower oil reduces the country's import bill, narrows the trade deficit, and alleviates upward pressure on inflation. The session opened at P61.76, meaning the currency strengthened throughout the trading day — a constructive sign of sustained demand for Peso. For FX traders, the key risk remains geopolitical: any re-escalation in the Middle East could quickly reverse these gains and push the Peso back toward — or beyond — record lows. Investors should monitor oil price developments closely, as well as any BSP commentary on FX intervention levels. The record-low print on Friday suggests the central bank may be watching carefully for disorderly market conditions.

high.title: T-Bill Yields Decline on Strong Investor Demand
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full P50 billion award at Monday's T-bill auction, with total tenders reaching P134.519 billion — nearly three times the amount on offer. Yields declined across all tenors, reflecting robust domestic investor appetite for short-duration government paper. The strong bid-to-cover ratio of approximately 2.7x signals significant liquidity in the system and a clear preference for short-term sovereign instruments. The easing of global oil prices and the associated improvement in sentiment appear to have supported the rally in T-bills, as lower inflation expectations reduce the risk premium demanded by investors. For bond investors, falling short-end yields may signal an eventual compression along the broader yield curve, particularly if the BSP maintains or shifts toward an easing bias. Traders should watch upcoming BSP policy meetings and inflation data to assess whether this demand momentum extends to longer tenors. The strong auction outcome is a positive signal for the government's near-term financing program.

high.title: Philippines Urged to Resolve Structural Issues to Draw More Foreign Investments
high.summary:
GlobalSource Partners has issued a stark warning that the Philippines must urgently address deep-rooted structural issues to reverse a deteriorating foreign direct investment (FDI) climate. Principal Advisor Diwa C. Guinigundo — a former BSP Deputy Governor — characterized the recent FDI slump as a "wake-up call," calling for credibility-restoring structural reforms. This is highly significant for PHP and Philippine asset markets: sustained FDI weakness implies reduced structural USD inflows, creating persistent downside pressure on the peso beyond near-term OFW remittance support. For bond investors, a weakening investment climate raises medium-term fiscal risk premia if revenue underperformance follows slower growth. Equity investors should note that foreign portfolio flows often track FDI sentiment directionally. Watch for: (1) any BSP commentary linking FDI trends to FX reserve adequacy; (2) legislative outcomes from the Marcos SONA proposals that could shift investor sentiment; and (3) next BSP balance of payments release for updated FDI data confirming or reversing the slump.

---

high.title: Peso Rises Further on Peace Deal Hopes
high.summary: The Philippine peso continued its appreciation run on Tuesday, gaining 6.1 centavos to close at P61.614/USD from Monday's P61.675 finish, according to Bankers Association of the Philippines data. The move was driven by two concurrent tailwinds: (1) declining global oil prices on growing optimism over a potential resolution to the Middle East conflict, which directly benefits the Philippines as a net oil importer and structurally supports the current account; and (2) a notably dovish-leaning signal from the BSP Governor, who indicated that more aggressive monetary action remains unlikely despite ongoing global market volatility. This latter point is critical for FX and rates traders — it suggests the BSP is comfortable holding its current policy stance, reducing the probability of emergency rate hikes that could disrupt the bond market. For PHP traders, the dual catalyst of lower oil (reduced import bill pressure) and a steady BSP posture is constructive near-term. Watch whether PHP can break and sustain below P61.50, which would represent a meaningful technical level. Oil price direction and any further BSP commentary remain the key variables.

high.title: BTr Fully Awards Dual-Tenor Bond Offering with Demand Exceeding 3x Supply
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) successfully raised the full P40 billion target in its dual-tranche Treasury bond auction on Tuesday, with total bids reaching P125.206 billion — more than three times the amount on offer, indicating exceptionally strong investor demand. Award rates were broadly aligned with prevailing secondary market yields, suggesting the market cleared without significant concession, a positive signal for the government's debt management program. The robust bid-to-cover ratio reflects improved risk appetite driven by easing Middle East geopolitical tensions and the associated decline in global oil prices, which reduce inflation fears and support duration positioning. For bond investors, the strong auction outcome signals that the domestic fixed income market remains well-bid, with investors willing to add Philippine government paper at current yield levels. This limits near-term upward pressure on yields and is supportive of mark-to-market performance for existing bond portfolios. Key watch points: the specific tenors awarded, the clearing yields relative to the secondary market curve, and whether this demand momentum carries into subsequent BTr auctions. A sustained bid-heavy environment could allow the BTr to price future issuances at tighter spreads.

high.title: BSP Chief Sees 'Small Chance' of Aggressive Tightening Amid Renewed Volatility
high.summary:
BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona, Jr. signaled on Tuesday that while the central bank sees only a "small chance" of more aggressive monetary policy tightening this year, the possibility of a larger 50-basis-point rate hike remains on the table amid fresh inflationary threats and renewed market volatility. The Governor's comments suggest the BSP is maintaining a cautiously hawkish bias, acknowledging that second-half economic recovery dynamics could reignite price pressures. For PHP traders, this is a critical signal: a 50bp hike scenario, even if low-probability, would be supportive of the peso and could attract short-term capital inflows seeking higher yields. For bond investors, the statement introduces upside risk to short-end yields, warranting vigilance on the 2–5 year segment of the GS curve. The market should watch upcoming inflation prints and any BSP policy meeting communications closely. If inflation surprises to the upside, the probability of aggressive tightening could reprice rapidly, steepening the front end of the yield curve and providing PHP support. Governor Remolona's tone underscores that the easing cycle is far from certain in the near term.

---

medium.title: BDO Q2 Net Income Slips 1.43% on Higher Loan Loss Provisioning
medium.summary:
BDO Unibank — the Philippines' largest bank by assets — reported a modest 1.43% decline in Q2 net income to P20.61 billion, dragged by higher loan loss provisioning and lower trading gains. First-half earnings edged up marginally to P40.72 billion from P40.62 billion a year ago, with ROE at 12.72% and ROA at 1.45%. The uptick in credit provisioning warrants monitoring as a potential signal of emerging asset quality stress in the broader lending portfolio. As a systemically important institution, BDO's credit cycle dynamics have implications for overall banking sector stability and the transmission of BSP monetary policy.

---

medium.title: Philippines to Be 4th Slowest-Growing ASEAN Economy This Year — AMRO
medium.summary: AMRO has held its Philippine GDP growth forecast unchanged at 4.1% for 2026 and 5.5% for 2027, positioning the Philippines as ASEAN's fourth slowest-growing economy this year. The agency cited heavy reliance on imported oil and a weak investment climate as key structural drags, with limited spillover from Middle East conflict as a relative silver lining. For FX traders, the below-regional-average growth trajectory reinforces a cautious PHP outlook — slower growth reduces the urgency for BSP to tighten policy, while imported oil dependence sustains structural USD demand and current account pressure. Bond investors should note that the 2027 growth acceleration assumption of 5.5% may be sensitive to reform delivery, making near-term government bond yields susceptible to downward revision risk if the fiscal consolidation path slips. This AMRO assessment also adds weight to the FDI structural concerns flagged by GlobalSource Partners.

medium.title: Philippine Banks' Assets Hit New High of P31 Trillion
medium.summary: BSP preliminary data shows the Philippine banking sector's combined assets reached a record P31.128 trillion as of end-June 2026, representing 10.34% year-on-year growth and a 2.25% month-on-month increase, surpassing the previous record of P30.442 trillion set in May. The asset base is primarily supported by loan growth, signaling continued credit expansion across the sector. For markets, robust banking sector balance sheet growth reflects underlying liquidity depth and supports PSEi financial sector valuations. From a monetary policy perspective, sustained credit expansion will be a key variable the BSP monitors when calibrating its easing or holding stance — strong loan growth may temper the case for further rate cuts. Bond market participants should watch whether expanding bank assets translate into increased appetite for government securities, which could provide technical support to GS prices.

medium.title: Marcos Pushes Tax Breaks and Reforms in SONA
medium.summary: President Marcos used his fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) to prioritize a legislative package including broader income tax exemptions for low- and middle-income earners and tax relief for MSMEs, alongside broader tax system modernization. While targeted at stimulating domestic consumption and improving the business environment, the fiscal implications are material for bond investors: income tax exemptions reduce government revenue, potentially widening the fiscal deficit and increasing gross borrowing requirements — a net negative for Philippine government bond supply-demand dynamics. PHP traders should monitor whether the market prices in higher fiscal risk premium on longer-dated GS. The reform agenda may, however, improve the medium-term FDI and investment climate if implemented credibly, offering a counterbalancing positive for PHP sentiment over time.

medium.title: AMRO Sees Philippines Posting Third Fastest Inflation in ASEAN+3 This Year
medium.summary: The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) revised its Philippine inflation forecast for 2026 down to 5.7% from a prior estimate of 6.0%, while maintaining its 2027 projection at 4.1%. Despite the downward revision, the Philippines is still projected to have the third-highest inflation rate among ASEAN+3 peers this year — a stark contrast to the 1.7% recorded in 2025, representing a significant acceleration. This inflationary backdrop is a critical constraint for BSP policy: elevated inflation relative to regional peers limits the central bank's room to ease aggressively, even as the Governor signaled against more aggressive tightening. For PHP and bond traders, persistently above-average inflation keeps real yields under pressure and may weigh on PHP carry attractiveness versus regional currencies. The 2027 deceleration to 4.1% provides some medium-term comfort, but the near-term inflation premium remains a risk factor to monitor closely alongside BSP's next policy decision.

medium.title: PSEi Climbs Back Above 6,300 as Middle East Tensions Ease
medium.summary: The PSEi rose 0.54% or 33.89 points to close at 6,314.90 on Monday, with the broader All Shares Index adding 0.37% to 3,435.37, as bargain hunting resumed amid de-escalating Middle East tensions and falling global oil prices. The recovery above the psychologically important 6,300 level is a modest positive technical signal for equity investors. Lower oil prices are a macro positive for the Philippines given its net oil import dependency, reducing cost pressures for corporate earnings and supporting consumer sentiment. The geopolitical risk-off unwind that drove this rally is the same catalyst behind peso strength and the strong BTr auction, reflecting a coherent macro risk-on environment across Philippine asset classes this week.

medium.title: Loan-to-Deposit Ratio May Drop Below 50% by 2050 as Population Ages
medium.summary:
An IMF working paper projects that the Philippines' loan-to-deposit (LDR) ratio could decline sharply from nearly 80% today to approximately 48% by 2050, driven by demographic aging as Filipino savers increasingly deposit rather than borrow. While the 2050 horizon is long-dated, this structural shift has meaningful implications for the banking sector's asset allocation and, by extension, the domestic bond market — a sustained rise in deposits relative to loans could channel more bank liquidity into Philippine government securities (GS), providing a structural bid for bonds. For international fund managers, this reinforces a constructive long-term outlook on Philippine GS demand dynamics. It also raises questions about future net interest margins for Philippine banks and the BSP's reserve management strategies as the deposit base expands structurally.

---

medium.title: Philippine Stocks Go Down on Last-Minute Selling
medium.summary:
The PSEi declined 0.17% (−10.87 points) to close at 6,304.03, while the broader All Shares Index fell 0.24% (−8.33 points) to 3,427.04. The selloff was driven by late-session profit-taking amid persistent geopolitical uncertainty and cautious sentiment surrounding corporate earnings prospects. Regional market weakness also weighed on local equities. For international fund managers, the modest decline suggests muted conviction on either side — bulls are not accumulating aggressively, but the downside remains contained. The 6,300 level is a key psychological support to watch; a sustained break below could signal further near-term weakness. Investors should monitor upcoming corporate earnings releases and any geopolitical developments that could amplify risk-off sentiment in the broader ASEAN region.

---
